title: Middle D Sings Again  (El re central vuelve a cantar)

segments.t: El martes por la mañana la lluvia por fin ha cesado sobre Portland. En la galería acristalada de la habitación nueve, Graham deja sus alicates finos junto al piano abierto mientras Evelyn toma asiento en el banco de madera. Escucha primero toda la escena.
The new felt bushing is dry and the brass pin sits tight, ma'am.
Your hands are as steady as a watchmaker's, Graham. May I try the key?
Go right ahead: gently first, then full weight.
Listen... D! Clear, round, and zero rattle in the wood!
Sounds a tiny bit flat next to the note above it, right?
You have a good ear, Graham! Turn the steel tuning wrench a hair to the right.
Right here... tell me when to stop.
Right... there! Hold it! Play a warm G major chord with me: listen!
Look at that: this old walnut box fills the whole glass room!
Wait until you hear Arthur's aunt's finished waltz tomorrow afternoon, Graham.
Let me screw the front panel back on and polish the brass pedals.
Thank you, Graham. After thirty quiet years, this piano has its voice back.
Repasemos paso a paso este momento delicado alrededor del viejo piano de nogal.
The new felt bushing is dry and the brass pin sits tight, ma'am.
'El fieltro nuevo del casquillo ya está seco y el pasador de latón encaja firme, señora.'
Your hands are as steady as a watchmaker's, Graham. May I try the key?
'Tiene usted un pulso tan firme como el de un relojero, Graham. ¿Puedo probar la tecla?'
Go right ahead: gently first, then full weight.
'Adelante, por supuesto: primero con suavidad y luego con todo el peso.'
Listen... D! Clear, round, and zero rattle in the wood!
'Escuche... ¡re! ¡Claro, redondo y sin el menor traqueteo en la madera!'
Sounds a tiny bit flat next to the note above it, right?
'Suena un poquitín baja al lado de la nota superior, ¿verdad?'
You have a good ear, Graham! Turn the steel tuning wrench a hair to the right.
'¡Tiene usted buen oído, Graham! Gire la llave de afinar de acero un pelo hacia la derecha.'
Right here... tell me when to stop.
'Justo aquí... dígame cuándo parar.'
Right... there! Hold it! Play a warm G major chord with me: listen!
'¡Justo... ahí! ¡Manténgalo! Toque conmigo un cálido acorde de sol mayor: ¡escuche!'
Look at that: this old walnut box fills the whole glass room!
'Mire eso: ¡esta vieja caja de nogal llena toda la sala acristalada!'
Wait until you hear Arthur's aunt's finished waltz tomorrow afternoon, Graham.
'Espere a oír mañana por la tarde el vals terminado de la tía de Arthur, Graham.'
Let me screw the front panel back on and polish the brass pedals.
'Déjeme atornillar de nuevo el panel frontal y sacar brillo a los pedales de latón.'
Thank you, Graham. After thirty quiet years, this piano has its voice back.
'Gracias, Graham. Después de treinta años en silencio, este piano ha recuperado su voz.'
Volvamos a escuchar completo a este dúo de afinadores.

You have a good ear, Graham! Turn the steel tuning wrench a hair to the right.
Right here... tell me when to stop.
Right... there! Hold it! Play a warm G major chord with me: listen!
Look at that: this old walnut box fills the whole glass room!
Wait until you hear Arthur's aunt's finished waltz tomorrow afternoon, Graham.
Let me screw the front panel back on and polish the brass pedals.
Thank you, Graham. After thirty quiet years, this piano has its voice back.
El re central suena limpio y afinado, y el piano vertical de nogal ya está listo para la gran tarde del miércoles. Hasta pronto.
Goodbye!
